create.title: Hard-TOP t=1 canonical close opposite-prime exchange sector
create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), y=floor(J), q_X=X/y^2, H=floor(yX^(-1/4)), and 1<<L<<H<=J^(1/2). Retain the literal squarefree t=1 scalar S_(L,1), its half-open N asymp L^2 shell, odd character-bearing divisor d, upper near-square window sqrt(N)<=d<=2sqrt(N), eta_L(d)Phi(d/(H+1))W(sqrt(q_X)d/(2sqrt(N))), even-N branch, floors, stars, endpoints, and zero extension. Fix kappa>0. For each supported squarefree N select canonically at most one pair of distinct odd prime divisors p_(N,L,kappa),q_(N,L,kappa) with chi_4(pq)=-1 and |log(q/p)|<=kappa L^(-1/2), using (N,L,kappa) but not the divisor allocation. Let S_(L,1)^cp be the complete incidence subsum where exactly one selected prime divides d. Exchanging p and q between d and N/d is an integral fixed-point-free multiplicity-one involution preserving N, squarefreeness, coprimality, oddness, the even-N branch, normalization, shell, and e(Jsqrt(N)), while reversing chi_4. On common smooth cells the accepted eta_L, Phi, W interfaces give amplitude difference O_kappa(L^(-1/2)); every cone, dyadic, profile, endpoint, star, ceiling, or zero-extension crossing lies in finitely many collars containing O_kappa(L^(3/2)+L) integer pairs. Hence |S_(L,1)^cp|<<_kappa L^(3/2), uniformly in the real centre. This proves no eligible-pair density, per-block nonemptiness, estimate for neither/both/no-pair incidences, or full t=1 target. A p congruent 3 mod 4 one-prime toggle has completely disjoint physical supports; averaging all such toggles, or any normalized family of sign-reversing full divisor-lattice involutions, returns the original coefficient exactly. Odd complement lies in the excluded lower window; for N=2M the physical complement is even and the odd-part complement lies in [sqrt(N)/4,sqrt(N)/2]. General matching, cycle, complement, and full-divisor identities are scoped route evidence only. No remaining channel, hard TOP parent, smooth packet, M9-M2, M9, bridge, target, or exponent follows.

reject.reason: The theorem selects at most one pair per product and proves no per-block nonemptiness, asymptotic density, positive proportion, or polynomial coverage.
No-pair products and every neither/both incidence remain in the unestimated residual scalar.
The physical interval has multiplicative width two while p>=3, so every one-prime sign-reversing partner lies outside.
Every active divisor reappears with its original sign once for each p congruent 3 modulo 4; normalized averaging is exact self-return.
A noninjective partner rule is not a reindexing; restricted exchange graphs still require sign-count equality and Hall's condition.
The complete bipartite sign graph has a perfect matching only when its two sign classes have equal size.
Even cycles and weighted transports only rewrite literal profile gradients and retain unmatched or same-sign fibres.
Odd complementation sends the upper interval to the excluded lower interval [sqrt(N)/2,sqrt(N)].
For N=2M the physical complement N/d is even, while the odd-part complement M/d lies in [sqrt(N)/4,sqrt(N)/2].
Full-divisor vanishing identifies the truncated coefficient with an uncontrolled profiled complement; it does not make the truncation small.
Logarithmic sparsity is L^(2-o(1)) at this scale and does not supply the missing L^(1/2-o(1)) gain.
Constant-profile and fixed-modulus prime-counting controls falsify combinatorial inferences but provide no lower bound for the literal weighted oscillatory scalar.
The residual t=1 incidences and the compatible L<<D<<L^2, t<<sqrt(L) channels remain open.
Balanced and unbalanced smooth packets have different owners, coefficients, and interfaces and receive no estimate from this hard-TOP incidence sector.
Both hard-TOP parents, both smooth M2 parents, M9-M2, M9-M1, endpoint uniformity, M9, and the unconditional bridge remain incomplete.
No parent theorem or bridge closes, so the internal one-third theorem and the external Li-Yang benchmark remain numerically unchanged.
